name: Dark current, read noise and x-ray response of a germanium CCD prototype (256 x 256, 8.1 um) at 94.7 K on an LN2-cooled cold plate below 5e-5 torr
plain_name: Check a new germanium camera chip for infrared astronomy while it sits at about 95 K
description: The MIT Lincoln Laboratory Ge-CCD GEDI7_-1_0 is mounted on an LN2-cooled cold plate inside a vacuum chamber at BNL (pressure below 5e-5 torr), cooled at no more than 3.5 K/min to a base of ~95 K with +/-0.03 K stability, and read out by an Archon controller; dark frames (1-20 s) at 94.69 K and x-ray pulse-height spectra are recorded.
keywords: Check a new germanium camera chip for infrared astronomy while it sits at about 95 K

sources.citation: S. C. Herrmann, 'Laboratory Characterization of a Ge-CCD Prototype for Future Near-Infrared Astronomical Instrumentation', arXiv:2610.22785 [hep-ex] (2026)

reported_equipment: BNL Ge-CCD test system: LN2-cooled cold plate in a vacuum chamber

requirements.rationale: Dark current and x-ray response are measured at 94.69 K.
The packaged device sits on a cold plate inside a vacuum chamber.
The chamber pressure was kept below 5e-5 torr during the measurements.
CCD clocks, biases and video output pass through the chamber to the Archon controller.
Optional: temperature was stable within +/-0.03 K during the dark-current measurements.
Optional: this test system cools the cold plate with liquid nitrogen.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
